candidates.description: A scale used to assess the functional status of cancer patients, where higher numbers indicate greater disability.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the numeric value associated with 'ECOG performance status' or 'Performance status: ECOG'.
candidates.measurement_definition: The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) scale, typically ranging from 0 (fully active) to 5 (dead).
candidates.name: ECOG Performance Status
candidates.uncertainty: The specific definitions for each grade are not provided in the text, relying on standard clinical knowledge of the ECOG scale.

citations.quote: PD‑L1 TPS 10%, and the patient’s ECOG 2 status

candidates.description: The percentage of viable tumor cells showing partial or complete membrane staining for PD-L1.
candidates.extraction_instruction: Extract the percentage value associated with 'PD-L1 TPS' or 'PD-L1 (22C3) IHC: Tumor proportion score'.
candidates.measurement_definition: Percentage value (0-100%) determined by immunohistochemistry (IHC), such as the 22C3 assay.
candidates.name: PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score (TPS)
candidates.uncertainty: The evidence only provides one value (10%) across different patients, limiting the range of observed variability.

limitations: Small number of patients described in the evidence.
Limited variability in the PD-L1 TPS values provided.
Lack of standardized reporting for some biomarkers across different patients.
summary: The provided evidence identifies baseline clinical and molecular markers in patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), specifically functional performance status (ECOG) and biomarker expression (PD-L1 Tumor Proportion Score), which are commonly associated with treatment selection and outcomes.
